land.text: the island under the US military government from 1 January 1899

successors.note: Cliopatria draws the whole of Cuba as US land in 1900-1904; the US dossier treats it as occupation.
The Republic of Cuba (this part) begins on 20 May 1902.

capitals.name: Camagüey (province; Jimaguayú and La Yaya assemblies)
capitals.note: The page gives no seat: the Council of Government 'operated in the field, relocating frequently'. The dot is the city of Camagüey; the assemblies of 16 September 1895 (Jimaguayú) and 10 October 1897 (La Yaya) were both in Camagüey province.

correction.text: Oriente, the eastern Cuba where the war was 'most prominent'

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws 56,428 km2 (Oriente and Camagüey, 252 cells: Granma 42, Santiago de Cuba 20, Guantánamo 32, Holguín 48, Las Tunas 34, Camagüey 64, Ciego de Ávila 8) for 1895-1897. The page has 'The insurrection began on February 24, 1895' with the war 'most prominent in Oriente' and 'By the end of June, all of Camagüey was at war', so the first months were Oriente alone; Camagüey enters by the ledger's June gain and the next keyframe. The Republic in Arms 'lacked control over stable territory, it functioned as a civil authority', so the shape is the zone of the insurrection, not a held state; neither page gives an area.

correction.text: Oriente and Camagüey as Cliopatria draws them

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1896-1897: the Cliopatria 1895 shape (Oriente and Camagüey) holds from June 1895. The page has the westward invasion ('invaded every province', 'arrived at the westernmost tip of the island on January 22, 1896') and Weyler's reconcentration, but no rebel-held land west of Camagüey, so the west is contested ground in the ledger, not rebel territory.

The same outline plus one cell (253 km2) on the north coast of Camagüey: grid noise. 'the U.S. military government, which had been installed on January 1, 1899' replaces Spain's rule across the island, including the rebel zone; the Representative Assembly dissolved on 4 April 1899.

region.text: Oriente, the eastern Cuba where the war was 'most prominent'

ledger.note: 24 February 1895: the Cuban insurrection begins in the east. 'The insurrection began on February 24, 1895.' 'The war was most prominent in Oriente, located in eastern Cuba.' Spain's Cliopatria shape keeps the whole island until 1894.

region.text: Camagüey, which 'was at war' by the end of June 1895

ledger.note: June 1895: the insurrection spreads to Camagüey. 'By the end of June, all of Camagüey was at war.' The page says at war, not held; Cliopatria draws Camagüey (and part of Ciego de Ávila) as rebel from 1895.

16 September 1895: the Republic in Arms gets a government. 'On 16 September 1895, delegates from the five main military commands of the Liberation Army forces adopted a constitution' at Jimaguayú, Camagüey; the Government Council was headed by Salvador Cisneros and Bartolomé Masó. The page gives no seat: the Council 'operated in the field, relocating frequently'.

region.text: the provinces west of Camagüey, which the revolutionaries invaded

ledger.note: 22 January 1896: the invasion reaches the west. 'The revolutionaries mounted a cavalry campaign that overcame the trochas and invaded every province'; 'they arrived at the westernmost tip of the island on January 22, 1896.' The west stays Spanish; Weyler's 'terror reached its height on October 21, 1896'.

region.text: the provinces west of Camagüey, which the revolutionaries invaded

ledger.note: 10 December 1898: Spain gives up the island. 'On December 10, 1898, the United States and Spain signed the Treaty of Paris' after the protocol of peace of 12 August 1898 (Congress had declared war on 25 April, Santiago surrendered on 16 July).

region.text: the rebel zone of Oriente and Camagüey

ledger.note: 4 April 1899: the Republic in Arms ends. 'the dissolution of the Representative Assembly on April 4, 1899'; 'the U.S. military government, which had been installed on January 1, 1899' already governed the island. The page gives no date for the disbanding of the Liberation Army (the Santa Cruz del Sur assembly of 24 October 1898 failed to demobilise it).

wars.outcome: The insurrection of 24 February 1895 ended with the United States' intervention in 1898: a protocol of peace on 12 August and the Treaty of Paris on 10 December 1898, followed by the US military government of 1 January 1899. The page gives no area changes.
wars.note: The page's infobox says independence was 'granted in 1902 Treaty of Paris' while its text dates the treaty to 1898. Spain's Cliopatria shape keeps the western half (252 cells) until 1899.

certainty.note: The rebel zone is where the insurrection operated, not held ground ('lacked control over stable territory'); no line is dated on the pages.

sources.title: Cuban War of Independence

sources.title: Republic of Cuba in Arms
sources.note: The Republic in Arms 1895-1899: constitution of 16 September 1895, no stable territory, military government 1 January 1899, Representative Assembly dissolved 4 April 1899; no seat, no area.

notes: Cliopatria's Wikipedia/Wikidata for this row (Fidel Castro, Q11256) are wrong: the row is the 1895-1899 insurrection, the Republic of Cuba in Arms; wikidata is left null and wikipedia gives the page used. Type rebel (rule 5): the Cuban War of Independence; the contested west (Spain's Cliopatria shape keeps 252 cells) is a contest zone, the held zone is the east. The page budget was 2 of 2. Not opened: the Spanish-American War page for the US side, the 'Government Council' presidents' dates (Cisneros 1895-1897, Masó 1897; Méndez Capote vice-president), the Pact of Zanjón (the earlier Republic in Arms of 1869-1878, outside Cliopatria's row). The Republic page says the Republic 'lacked control over stable territory', so every border here is soft. Cliopatria's USA row draws 8 cells at Guantánamo and Santiago in 1898-1899 (US landings), which belong to the US dossier. Counterparts: kingdom-of-spain (eu-12), united-states-of-america (am-07), republic-of-cuba (this part).
